goal: The goal is to provide useful information for tourists, residents of Oslo, and nearby cities.
important_tips: Important tips and advice to help you explore Oslo, including county maps provided by the Ruter app:
look_at_metro: What to pay attention to when traveling by metro using the Ruter app:
tip_0: Download the correct version of the app, otherwise you won’t be able to buy tickets or check public transport routes. Alternatively, you can buy a card at a Ruter service point, top it up, and validate it on the correct metro line.
tip_1: Regarding central Oslo stations (Nationaltheatret, Jernbanetorget, Stortinget), the first two provide access to metro, trains, and buses.
tip_2: All metro lines operate within zone 1, except line 3, but the ticket for line 3 is the same as for other metro lines.
tip_3: Student IDs (Polish) are accepted in the Ruter app.
tip_4: In Oslo, there are always two metro trains on line number 5 running in opposite directions: "Sognsvann" and "Ringen via Tøyen".

emergency_facility: In exceptional situations such as continuous delays or traffic suspension, it is recommended to follow the Ruter app and listen to station announcements. If the situation affects you significantly, for example if you are unable to get home and have no other option, you may consider ordering a taxi. Ruter may reimburse the cost after submitting a receipt and explanation.
fine_info: The fine for traveling without a valid ticket is 1237 NOK if paid on the spot. If paid later, the amount is 1437 NOK.
look_at_trikk: What to pay attention to when traveling by tram using the Ruter app:
tip_5: Trams in Oslo tend to be delayed, so it’s recommended to allow extra time if they are used as a connecting transport.
tip_6: A recurring issue is that lines disappear from departure boards and the Ruter app, usually followed by a few minutes of delay.
tram_distribution: Tram table within the Oslo area
look_at_train: What to pay attention to when traveling by train with the Ruter # app:
look_at_tog_wogn_0: Train carriages are marked as regular, accessible, for parents with strollers, and quiet zones. Always pay attention to which carriage you enter.
look_at_tog_wogn_1: Carriages also have large stickers on the doors (Valid ticket / Gyldig billett), which means you must have an active ticket to avoid extra charges.
tip_8: When public transport services such as trains operated by Ruter, Vy, or Flytoget are suspended, replacement transport is usually organized as quickly as possible, most often buses. Unfortunately, the Ruter app does not always provide good real-time information about sudden changes.
tip_9: Very often the app is not updated, so you must rely on departure boards or announcements. If you have already purchased a train ticket, it may unfortunately become invalid.

look_at_bus: What to pay attention to when traveling by bus using the Ruter app:
tip_10: Make sure you are standing at the correct bus stop. In Oslo, bus stops are often placed in a row or in different directions and marked with letters (A–F). An exception is bus terminals, where buses must stop at designated platforms.
tip_11: In Norway, it is common that the bus will not stop unless you signal the driver, for example by waving.
tip_12: Bus drivers in Oslo and Bærum often drive abruptly, so it is recommended to stand up only after the bus has stopped.

ekebergparken: A park with beautiful sculptures and views over Oslo. Tram line 18 to the Ekebergparken stop.
frogner_park: Famous for Gustav Vigeland’s sculptures, ideal for walks and relaxation. Tram line 12 to Vigelandsparken.
sognsvann: A popular place for walking, jogging, and picnics. Metro line 5 to Sognsvann.
holmenkollen: Ski jump with a ski museum and panoramic views of Oslo. Metro line 1 to Holmenkollen.
nordmarka: A vast forest area ideal for hiking, cycling, and cross-country skiing. Metro line 1 to Frognerseteren.
tryvann_vinterpark: A ski resort with downhill slopes. Metro line 1 to Voksenkollen, then shuttle bus. Located near Tryvannstua.
wyspy_oslofjord: Places for swimming and picnics. Ferry lines 91–94 from Rådhusbrygge operated by Oslo-Fergene.
bygdoy: A peninsula with museums and beaches. Bus line 30 to Bygdøynes.
